title: Control heuristics scratch - Silas
content:
Purpose: quick brain-dump of control heuristics, evidence pointers, and open questions for SOC2-like readiness. Meant to be messy; will formalize later.

Topline thoughts:
- Focus on mapping runtime features -> control families. Redwood-specific items: token-level cost/latency logs, per-route dashboards, canary rollouts, KV cache behaviors, dedicated vs hosted isolation notes, KMS/HSM integrations.
- Evidence should be lightweight but repeatable (scripts to pull traces, screenshots with exact query IDs, short runbook steps).

Mapping sketch (rough):
- CC1 (Org & Comms): ownership docs (team roster), incident comms template (slack + email flows), retention policy (console retention settings). Evidence: staff list export, comms playbook draft. TODO: ask HR for up-to-date hires export (JIRA: HR-44).
- CC2 (Change mgmt / PR controls): deployment gates, canary rollouts, rollback logs. Evidence: GitHub PRs + deploy tags; link to infra PR above. Note: make small script to snapshot deploy window (git sha + k8s rollout).
- CC3 (Access controls): RBAC in console, operator access routines, ephemeral keys for SRE. Evidence: sample role bindings, KMS access logs. Open Q: who owns operator-access-review cadence? (ping: @Ava)
- CC4 (Data protection & encryption): KMS usage for keys, TLS everywhere, s3 bucket policies for model artifacts, KV cache encryption note (does runtime encrypt KV at rest?). Action: confirm with infra (Rohan).
- CC5 (Monitoring & incident mgmt): traces, replayable alerts, runbooks. Evidence: per-route tracing screenshot + extraction script. TODO: write a 1-pager: "How to pull token-level latency spike for a customer".
- CC6 (Business continuity): dedicated capacity SLA docs, fallback routing policies (hosted->dedicated->private). Evidence: traffic routing config snapshot, DR plan doc.

Evidence collection heuristics (practical):
- Prefer scripts over manual screenshots. e.g., curl -> /admin/logs?run=abc -> save json -> redact -> store in evidence bucket.
- When screenshot unavoidable include exact query parameters and timestamp.
- Annotate evidence with control ID + short narrative: what it demonstrates, who validated it, when.

Questions / unknowns (to resolve):
- Do runtime KV caches persist long-term or ephemeral per-request? impact on data classification and retention. (Action: Rohan check on runtime-cache TTLs)
- Where are service account credentials rotated? monthly? quarterly? Currently I only know about KMS key rotation schedule but not service-account tokens.
- Policy for third-party model providers (are they considered subservice orgs for SOC2 scoping?). Need legal guidance. (Linked artifact: CONFLUENCE-9876)

Immediate next steps (short):
- Draft small checklist per CC family with 3 evidence items each (DUE: 2026-03-16).
- Create automated evidence puller (python script): pulls last 30 days of deploy tags, RBAC export, and TLS cert expiry -> attach to playbook. (owner: Silas)
- Quick sync with Rohan + Ava to confirm cache/TLS/KMS facts (calendar invite).

Notes-to-self (random):
- Keep naming consistent: evidence IDs as EVID-<CC#>-<n>.
- When in doubt, capture more telemetry rather than less. storage cost < failing audit.
- Use redaction checklist before uploading any logs to shared drive (PII, customer prompts).

Scratch ideas for control narratives (one-liners to rework later):
- "Automated deploy gates ensure only reviewed code reaches canary clusters; rollback automated on SLA breach."
- "RBAC restrictions enforced at API gateway + console; operator sessions require MFA and ephemeral keys."
- "KV cache does not persist customer prompt text beyond configured TTL; runtime strips PII fields before caching."

Random drafts & fragments:
- "If we can show a 30-day history of deploys + canary success rate and attach a runbook, that covers much of change mgmt evidence."
- "Need legal to sign off on subservice narrative re: open model weights (are they store-of-record?)."

End of dump. Will clean up and move into a proper per-control spreadsheet once the checklist draft stabilizes.
